previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a suprapubic catheter, was admitted for a right percutaneous nephrolithotomy due to bilateral kidney stones. The procedure was performed without complications, and a temporary nephrostomy tube was placed on the right side. He received intravenous antibiotics for 24 hours and was transitioned to oral pain control with acetaminophen and a narcotic for breakthrough pain. The right nephrostomy tube was clamped and subsequently removed on postoperative day one after he remained pain-free. He tolerated a regular diet, had stable labs, and no signs of infection. He was discharged home with instructions to care for the remaining left nephrostomy tube, continue fosfomycin, monitor for complications, and prepare for the left-sided procedure in the coming weeks.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o man w/ MS ___ neurogenic bladder s/p 
suprapubic catheter and recurrent UTIs with MDR organisms now 
presenting with recurrent UTI.  

# Complicated UTI with sepsis: The patient presented with 
leukocytosis, fever, and likely urinary tract infection. He has 
had multiple prior admissions for UTI with cultures growing MDR 
sensitive to linezolid and meropenem. Urinalysis revealed 162 
WBC's, ___, positive nitrites and bacteria. Patient was initially 
treated with Meropenem and Linezolid in the ED, but transitioned 
to Vanc/Zosyn on the floor. Fevers resolved and WBC normalized. 
Culture revealed ___ Ecoli, sensitive to Bactrim, so patient 
was transitioned to Bactrim on ___. Renal US showed no 
hydronephrosis. Patient's suprapubic tube was changed by Urology 
on ___ and he was discharged home with instructions to complete 
10 day course of antibiotics (last day ___. He will follow 
up with PCP. 

# Hypoxemia: Patient was initially placed on 4L in the ED, given 
concern for hypoxemia. Given unimpressive CXR and the fact that 
the patient is bed bound and was breathing so comfortably on 
arrival to the floor, this was attributed to atelectasis. 
Patient able to be weaned off O2 and subjective dyspnea 
resolved.

# Dysphagia: There was initially concern for aspiration in the 
setting of dysphagia, as patient presented with dyspnea and new 
oxygen requirement in ED. He was evaluated by S&S on ___, 
determined ok for ground diet and thin liquids. 
  
# Sacral Decubitus Ulcer: Patient had stage 1 ulcer on his 
sacrum. He was followed closely by wound care during admission. 

# HLD:  
- Continued ezetimibe  

# Neurogenic bladder:
- Continued oxybutynin  

# Chronic pain:  
- Continued oxycodone PRN 

# GERD:  
- Continued omeprazole
